subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a temp artifact provenance and cleanup model, and where is the boundary between core runtime guardrails, SQLite-backed provenance, plugin SDK seams, and ClawHub workflow packages?
rationale: The safety goal fits current priorities, but implementing it changes storage ownership, cleanup authority, agent/tool APIs, doctor checks, and core-vs-plugin boundaries that automation should not choose by itself.

options.title: Core guardrails plus provenance seam
options.body: Core would add runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving audit/review workflow classes to plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core temp registry
options.body: Core would own a complete temp artifact registry and cleanup/janitor policy for all first-class OpenClaw temp outputs, accepting broader storage and cleanup responsibility.

options.title: Plugin-only workflow solution
options.body: Core would keep existing temp-root hardening and require janitor/audit provenance behavior to be packaged outside core unless a concrete missing plugin API is found.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus provenance seam
recommendation.body: Core would add runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving audit/review workflow classes to plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest overlap across temp-boundary hardening, security docs, plugin/core boundary policy, and previous product-scope review context.
